SLOOS-informed modification: The July 27, 2022 FOMC statement is clearly hawkish (75 bp hike to 2.25–2.50%, guidance for “ongoing increases,” and balance-sheet runoff ramping to $60B Treasuries/$35B MBS per month in September). However, the July 2022 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows bank credit conditions were already tightening materially: banks tightened standards for C&I loans across firm sizes and for CRE and most residential mortgage categories (including GSE-eligible and jumbo), as well as for credit cards and auto loans; they increased loan pricing and collateral requirements; and cited a weaker economic outlook and lower risk tolerance. Demand was mixed—stronger for C&I and HELOCs, but weaker for CRE and many RRE categories. This tighter bank-intermediation backdrop implies additional restraint on growth and inflation via the credit channel, modestly tempering the net hawkish tone of the FOMC statement relative to an FSR-only read. Net: still hawkish, but with a stronger drag from bank credit tightening.
